title: Non-invasive intracranial pressure estimation in the intensive care unit: narrative review of methods and clinical applications
one_line_summary: Non-invasive intracranial pressure estimation modalities complement invasive monitoring by providing bedside screening, risk stratification, and physiological monitoring across neurocritical, general ICU, emergency, and low-resource settings.
key_pearls: Non-invasive intracranial pressure (**nICP**) estimators cannot replace invasive probes due to lack of zeroing/calibration, exhibiting *95% limits of agreement* of **±7–15 mmHg** for TCD and **±7–10 mmHg** for ONSD.

A Transcranial Doppler pulsatility index (**PI**) **≥ 1.4** or **> 1.5** (in the absence of arterial hypotension and hypocapnia) with end-diastolic velocity (**EDV**) **≤ 20 cm/s** strongly indicates intracranial hypertension (**IH**).
An optic nerve sheath diameter (**ONSD**) threshold of **≥ 5.8–6.0 mm** (measured 3 mm retrobulbar) yields an *83% sensitivity and specificity* for identifying elevated ICP.

Automated pupillometry with a Neurological Pupil Index (**NPi**) **< 3** reflects midbrain compression from uncal herniation, while **NPi ≤ 2** within 6 hours post-cardiac arrest strongly predicts poor neurological outcome.
Cranial microdeformation analysis (*brain4care*) provides continuous compliance assessment, where a **P2/P1 ratio ≥ 1.4** and time-to-peak **TTP ≥ 0.3** identify **IH** with **90% specificity**.
The **B-ICONIC** consensus recommends combining at least two complementary **nICP** modalities alongside clinical examination and imaging rather than relying on a single technique.
population: Critically ill adult and pediatric patients with acute brain injury or at risk of secondary brain injury from intracranial hypertension

sections.heading: Introduction and Principles of nICP Monitoring
sections.content:
- Intracranial hypertension (**IH**) post-acute brain injury (**ABI**) drives secondary brain damage, requiring continuous physiology-driven intracranial pressure (**ICP**) surveillance.
- Direct invasive methods (**intraparenchymal probes** and **external ventricular drains [EVD]**) remain the gold standard with an accuracy of **±2 mmHg** in the **0–20 mmHg** range.
- **nICP** estimators serve primarily as high *negative predictive value (NPV)* screening tools to rule out **IH**, guide patient selection for invasive probes, and monitor patients with contraindications (e.g., severe coagulopathy).
- High sensitivity and specificity are mutually exclusive; highly sensitive screening risks over-placement of invasive probes, whereas high specificity risks missing elevated ICP.
- The **B-ICONIC** consensus highlights that no single **nICP** technique is sufficient; integrating at least two distinct modalities with clinical and radiological parameters is **recommended**.
section_pearls: Invasive ICP monitors require accuracy within **±2 mmHg** (**0–20 mmHg**), which no current non-invasive tool can match.
nICP tools excel as high negative predictive value rule-out instruments rather than single-point numerical proxies.

sections.heading: Transcranial Doppler Ultrasound Methods
sections.content:
- Transcranial Doppler (**TCD**) measures blood flow velocity in basal cerebral arteries (primarily the middle cerebral artery [**MCA**]).
- Elevated **ICP** reduces cerebral perfusion pressure (**CPP**) and increases **critical** closing pressure (**CrCP**), preferentially reducing end-diastolic flow velocity (**EDV** or **FVd**) and increasing the pulsatility index (**PI**).
- **PI** is calculated as **(PSV - EDV) / MV**; an optimal cut-off value of **1.28** yields a *sensitivity and specificity* of **0.74**.
- Empirical formulas derive non-invasive CPP (**nCPP = MAP * [FVd / FVm] + 14**) and non-invasive ICP (**nICP = MAP - nCPP**); a threshold of **nICP > **19.6 mmHg**** or **> **25 mmHg**** signals **IH** (*sensitivity 0.70, specificity 0.70*).
- *95% limits of agreement* for TCD-derived ICP range from **±7 mmHg** to **±15 mmHg**, with mean **absolute** errors around **9.5 mmHg** (reduced to **3.9 mmHg** using domain-adversarial neural networks).
- Confounders altering **PI** independently of true ICP include mean arterial pressure (**MAP**), heart rate, **PaCO2/ETCO2**, arterial stiffness, cerebral vasospasm, and sedative administration.
- Severe **IH** progressing toward cerebral circulatory arrest demonstrates characteristic TCD stages: reverberating flow, systolic spikes, and total disappearance of flow signal.
section_pearls: A **PI > 1.5** without hypotension or hypocapnia strongly indicates elevated ICP.
TCD empirical formulas demonstrate 95% limits of agreement of **±7–15 mmHg**.

sections.heading: Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter Ultrasonography
sections.content:
- The optic nerve sheath (**ONS**) is continuous with the intracranial subarachnoid space; the trabeculated 3 mm retrobulbar region expands dynamically as **ICP** rises.
- **ONSD** values **< 5.2 mm** are considered normal, **5.2–5.8 mm** represent a grey zone requiring repeat testing/multimodal correlation, and **> 5.8–6.0 mm** indicate **IH**.
- An optimal **ONSD** threshold of **5.9 mm** yields a *sensitivity* of **0.83** and *specificity* of **0.83** (*95% limits of agreement* range **±7–10 mmHg**).
- Standardized acquisition via the **CLOSED** protocol (*Color Doppler, Low power, Optic disk clarity, Safety/short duration, Elevate frequency, Dual measurements*) eliminates technical artifacts.
- Internal sheath diameter (**ONSDint**, subarachnoid space only) differs from external sheath diameter (**ONSDext**, including dura) by approximately **22%**, necessitating clear definition in serial tracking.
- Acoustic exposure must follow the *ALARA* principle to protect the lens and retina; measurements must be consistent across repeats (*< 10% inter-measurement difference*).
section_pearls: Retrobulbar **ONSD ≥ 6.0 mm** reliably identifies intracranial hypertension.
Internal versus external ONSD measurements introduce an approximate **22%** size discrepancy.

sections.heading: Automated Quantitative Pupillometry
sections.content:
- Quantitative pupillometry measures pupillary light reflex (**PLR**) parameters: pupil size, percentage constriction (**%C**), constriction velocity (**CV**), maximum constriction velocity (**MCV**), dilation velocity (**DV**), and latency.
- The Neurological Pupil Index (**NPi**) and Quantitative Pupillometry Index (**QPi**) scale reactivity from **0 to 5**; an **NPi < 3** is considered abnormal.
- An optimal **NPi** cut-off value of **3.96** yields a *sensitivity* of **0.68** and *specificity* of **0.68** for detecting **IH**.
- **NPi** drops precede transtentorial/uncal herniation and midbrain compression, but show weak correlation with **absolute** numerical **ICP** in the absence of brainstem displacement.
- In post-cardiac arrest hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (**HIE**), an **NPi ≤ 2** within **6 hours** post-resuscitation strongly predicts poor 90-day neurological outcomes with high specificity at **72 hours**.
section_pearls: An **NPi < 3** signals midbrain/oculomotor nerve compression requiring immediate evaluation.
Post-cardiac arrest **NPi ≤ 2** within **6 hours** strongly predicts poor neurological recovery.

sections.heading: Cranial Microdeformation and Non-invasive Compliance Methods
sections.content:
- The *brain4care* (**B4C**) system uses a wearable cranial extensometer to detect beat-to-beat micrometric skull expansion (**< 0.2 µm** resolution) corresponding to intracranial pressure waveform (**ICPW**) morphology.
- Key pulse wave morphology parameters include the tidal-to-percussion peak ratio (**P2/P1 ratio**) and normalized time-to-peak (**nTTP**).
- A **P2/P1 ratio ≤ 0.8** rules out **IH** (**ICP > 20 mmHg**) with a *sensitivity* of **0.92** and *specificity* of **0.19**.
- A **P2/P1 ratio ≥ 1.4** combined with an **nTTP ≥ 0.30** confirms depleted intracranial compliance and **IH** with a *specificity* of **0.90** (*sensitivity 0.11–0.16*).
- Integrated machine learning models processing cranial expansion waveforms estimate **absolute** **ICP** with mean errors near **3 mmHg**.
- Other secondary **nICP** modalities include optic coherence tomography (**OCT/OCTA**) for optic disc swelling, tympanic membrane displacement (**TMD**), acoustic ultrasound time-of-flight (**TOF**), two-depth ophthalmic artery Doppler, and CT/MRI-derived elastance indices.
section_pearls: Cranial pulse wave **P2/P1 ratio ≤ 0.8** reliably rules out ICP **> 20 mmHg** (*sensitivity 0.92*).
A **P2/P1 ratio ≥ 1.4** and **nTTP ≥ 0.3** indicate severely exhausted intracranial compliance (*specificity 0.90*).

sections.heading: Clinical Applications across Neuro-ICU and General ICU Settings
sections.content:
- **Neuro-ICU Application**: **nICP** refines patient selection for invasive monitors in severe **TBI** or **SAH** (where only ~33% develop sustained **IH**), provides interim surveillance during active coagulopathy/anticoagulation, and assists decision-making in moderate **TBI**.
- **Post-Cardiac Arrest**: Ischemia-reperfusion edema causes **IH**; **TCD PI ≥ 1.49** and elevated **ONSD** correlate with post-resuscitation **IH** and poor neurological recovery.
- **Acute Liver Failure (ALF)**: Cerebral edema affects ~**30%** of **ALF** cases where invasive probes carry high bleeding risks; pediatric **ONSD > 4.55–4.6 mm** accurately identifies raised **ICP** and failure to drop below **4.6 mm** at **24 hours** predicts **mortality**.
- **Acute Respiratory Failure & ARDS**: High positive end-expiratory pressure (**PEEP**) causing alveolar overdistension raises intrathoracic pressure and **ICP**; **TCD** guides individual PEEP titration and **30° head-up reverse-Trendelenburg** prone positioning to prevent spikes in **PI** and **nICP**.
- **Sepsis**: An **ONSD > 5.2 mm** and impaired cerebral autoregulation on **TCD** predict sepsis-associated encephalopathy (**SAE**).
section_pearls: In acute liver failure, **nICP** provides critical surveillance when invasive probes are contraindicated due to coagulopathy.
In ARDS with brain injury, 30° head-up positioning during prone positioning prevents deleterious ICP elevations.

sections.heading: Pre-hospital, Emergency, Low-Resource, and Austere Environments
sections.content:
- Classical Cushing's reflex signs (*hypertension, bradycardia, irregular respiration*) have poor sensitivity for early **IH** in pre-hospital settings.
- Automated pupillometry and cranial extensometry enable rapid, hands-free assessment within **1 minute** during transport or emergency department triage.
- In low- and middle-income countries (**LMICs**) lacking neurosurgical facilities, validated imaging and clinical protocols (**ICE**, **CREVICE**, **BOOTStraP**) combined with serial **nICP** ultrasound improve care without invasive monitors.
- In military combat casualty and austere care, Joint Trauma System (**JTS**) clinical practice guidelines incorporate automated pupillometry (**NPi < 3**) for **TBI** field triage.
section_pearls: Automated pupillometry (**NPi < 3**) is formally integrated into military deployed CPGs for combat TBI triage.
Non-invasive tools facilitate structured protocols (CREVICE/ICE) in low-resource environments lacking neurosurgery.

strengths_limitations:
- Strengths: Non-invasive, safe, portable bedside evaluation that enables rapid screening, risk stratification, and longitudinal tracking across diverse clinical environments (ICU, ED, LMICs, combat).
- Limitations: Lack of continuous calibration and zeroing prevents direct replacement of invasive probes; methods display broad 95% limits of agreement (±7–**15 mmHg**), **notable** operator dependency, and an inability to quantify cumulative temporal ICP pressure-time burden ("ICP dose").
